EBITDA.note: AMBIGUITY #1 (see step-7 list). Bound to the model's single pinned EBITDA bridge row ('Reported EBITDA') per the standard contract -- do not recompute a different EBITDA. Independently re-verified (not merely copied from a prior pass) against every monthly package from 2024-09 through 2026-06 (22 of 22 months checked): the borrower's own CERTIFIED 'Covenant EBITDA' (Portfolio Monitoring/<quarter>/Covenant Calculation.xlsx TTM Detail 'EBITDA' column, identical every quarter to the matching Compliance Certificate's 'CALCULATION' figure) equals this Reported-EBITDA bridge row PLUS A CONSTANT $553,353.26/month ($6,640,239.12/year), to the penny, in EVERY month checked -- spanning the Predecessor, Legacy, AND A&R agreements alike, so it is not a restructuring-era or A&R-specific feature. NONE of the nine executed documents read for this extraction (A&R Agreement, Legacy Credit Agreement, Exit Amendment, Predecessor Credit Agreement, Guaranty and Security Agreement, Fee Letter, Closing Officer Certificate, Funding Request, Solvency Certificate) states an EBITDA add-back, an operating-lease/rent add-back, or any other reconciling item in words. The only place a similarly-sized figure appears in writing anywhere in the deal folder is Restructuring/Closing Materials/Goodwill Impairment Support.xlsx ('Lease Basis Demonstration' tab: '2025 facility lease expense included above' = $6,640,239.12 = $553,353.26 x 12) -- an UNRELATED ASC 350 goodwill-impairment DCF workpaper (not an executed loan document, not a compliance schedule), whose own stated conclusion is the OPPOSITE of an addback ('Post-rent cash flows and no lease-liability addback; no double count'). That figure also does NOT match the borrower's actual disclosed monthly lease cash payments (operating-support.xlsx 'Leases' tab: $546,675.00/month in 2026, $534,608.07/month in early 2025, both escalating) -- the $553,353.26 gap is INVARIANT every single month, which real lease cash flows are not. CONCLUSION OF THIS EXTRACTION: the reconciling constant is real and precisely quantifiable in the certified exhibits, but this extraction could NOT verify it traces to agreement text, so it is recorded here as a NOTE only and is NOT folded into 'compute' (per the hard rule that a borrower/certificate add-back the agreement does not support stays out of the EBITDA definition). Net effect: a TTM FCCR reconstructed off this spec's EBITDA will run BELOW the borrower's own certified Covenant EBITDA by $553,353.26/month x 12 = $6,640,239.12 TTM understated. Since the only covenant that reads this definition (FCCR) is currently SUSPENDED (informational only), this does not misstate an active compliance determination today, but must be resolved -- against a longer-form agreement if one exists, or by an explicit analyst election -- before the FCCR is ever reactivated or quoted as anything more than a rough approximation.

covenants.note: STATUS AS OF THIS EXTRACTION (2026-09-15 knowledge date): SUSPENDED, INFORMATIONAL ONLY. Origin: introduced at 1.2000x quarterly TTM by the Legacy Credit Agreement effective 2025-01-15 ('FCCR' section) and ACTIVELY TESTED AND COMPLIANT for three quarters (2025-Q1 1.7322x, 2025-Q2 1.7755x, 2025-Q3 1.4273x, each 'Governing disposition: COMPLIANT'). SUSPENDED (informational only, expressly 'not deemed compliant or waived') by the Exit Amendment effective 2025-12-05 ('STABILIZATION PERIOD' / 'RESERVATION OF RIGHTS' sections: 'The legacy FCCR Test is SUSPENDED through December 31, 2026 ... The suspension is not a waiver, amendment of the 1.2000x threshold, or compliance determination'). The A&R Agreement (effective 2026-03-31) CONTINUES this suspension UNCHANGED through the same December 31, 2026 date ('COVENANT DISPOSITION' section) -- it does not reinstate, waive, or replace the test with a different one; it is the SAME suspended legacy covenant carried forward, not a new A&R-native covenant. Every quarter since suspension (2025-Q4 through 2026-Q2) shows 'Test applicability: SUSPENDED' / 'Governing disposition: SUSPENDED' alongside an informational 'Economic state: WOULD BREACH' calculation that has WORSENED every quarter (2025-Q4 1.0478x; 2026-Q1 0.6687x; 2026-Q2 0.3682x -- all below 1.2000x). AMBIGUITY #2 (see step-7 list) -- REINSTATEMENT: Stabilization Milestones.xlsx names Milestone M4 ('Deliver FCCR reinstatement readiness analysis', owner CFO, due 2026-09-30, status PENDING as of the June 2026 package). On the face of the documents made available this is a DELIVERABLE (an analysis to be produced), not a stated automatic-reinstatement trigger, level, or mechanism. This spec's threshold_schedule nonetheless assumes reinstatement at the original 1.2000x level effective 2027-01-01, immediately upon expiry of the suspension window, because the A&R's own wording bounds the suspension to a date certain ('through December 31, 2026') rather than stating it continues until further amendment. The alternative reading -- that suspension persists past 2026-12-31 absent a further amendment/waiver (consistent with the Exit Amendment's own 'reservation of rights' language), or that M4's analysis could itself reset the reinstatement date or level -- is equally supportable and is the analyst's call. Given the deeply sub-1.0x and worsening informational trend (0.3682x TTM at June 2026), and the further EBITDA/Fixed-Charges definitional gaps noted above, a mechanical reinstatement at 1.2000x on 2027-01-01 would very likely register as an immediate breach.

decisions.question: Does the constant $553,353.26/month gap between Reported EBITDA and the borrower's certified 'Covenant EBITDA' belong in the EBITDA definition's compute block?
options_considered: Accept as parsed: exclude the add-back, bind EBITDA to Reported EBITDA only, keep the reconciliation as a note
Fold the $553,353.26/month add-back into compute since it reproduces the certified figure exactly
decisions.decision: Accept as parsed: exclude the add-back
decisions.rationale: The extractor swept all nine executed documents and found no add-back language anywhere; the one document with a matching dollar figure (Goodwill Impairment Support.xlsx) is an unrelated ASC 350 workpaper whose own conclusion is 'no lease addback taken' -- the opposite of what it would be cited for. Folding an unsupported number into a covenant definition is a bigger error than leaving a documented gap, especially since the only covenant that reads this definition (FCCR) is currently suspended. Reopen this once a longer-form credit agreement or an actual EBITDA-definition exhibit is located.

decisions.question: Should Fixed_Charges be broadened to match the certified TTM figure (interest + principal + leases + maintenance capex), or held to facility debt service only?
options_considered: Accept as parsed: facility cash interest + scheduled principal only (per the standard template reading)
Broaden to include lease payments and maintenance capex to match the certificate
decisions.decision: Accept as parsed: facility debt service only
decisions.rationale: No lease-payment or maintenance-capex model row exists in this borrower's canonical model (borrower-config model_lines has no such lines), and no agreement text defines Fixed Charges beyond the one FCCR sentence. Matching the certified figure would require inventing rows and a formula the agreement doesn't support. The ~$9.1M TTM gap is disclosed in the definition's note so nobody mistakes this reconstruction for the certified number.

decisions.question: Does the FCCR reinstate at 1.2000x on 2027-01-01, or does the suspension persist indefinitely pending a further amendment / the M4 deliverable?
options_considered: Accept as parsed: assume mechanical reinstatement at 1.2000x effective 2027-01-01, since the suspension text is bounded to a date certain ('through December 31, 2026')
Leave open-ended: suspension continues past 2026-12-31 absent a further amendment, consistent with the Exit Amendment's 'reservation of rights' language
decisions.decision: Accept as parsed: keep the 2027-01-01 / 1.2000x schedule entry, but treat it as a forward-stress marker rather than a confirmed compliance date
decisions.rationale: The A&R's own wording bounds the suspension to a date certain rather than 'until further amendment,' so the literal reading supports reinstatement absent new action. But this is explicitly NOT a confident reading -- Milestone M4 (due 2026-09-30, ~2 weeks from today) is only a 'deliver a reinstatement-readiness analysis' deliverable, not a stated trigger, and the informational FCCR is deeply sub-1.0x and worsening (0.3682x at June 2026). Left OPEN for analyst review: this is the single highest-priority open item on this credit and should be revisited immediately once the M4 analysis is delivered or a further amendment is executed -- do not let the monitor quietly assume compliance resumes on 2027-01-01 without an analyst sign-off closer to that date.

decisions.question: Accept the engine's flat, original-principal-base amortization and actual/360 day-count approximation, knowing it will not tie to certified declining-balance / flat-30/360 figures?
options_considered: Accept as parsed: use the flat approximation, reconcile to certificates by hand each quarter
Hold the debt-service schedule entirely and read only the certified exhibits
decisions.decision: Accept as parsed: use the generated schedule for interest/principal timing and covenant-support-row structure, but read the certified Covenant Calculation exhibits as the governing figures for actual cash interest and scheduled principal each quarter
decisions.rationale: Same class of engine limitation already accepted for Nemeris. The gap is fully quantified and documented (engine ~$150/month interest gap in three of three months checked; principal gap grows from $0 to material by later years) -- not a data error, a v1 engine capability gap. Facility Cash Interest Expense / Facility Scheduled Debt Principal Payments should be populated from the certified figures where available, per assembling-rules, with the generated schedule as fallback for months no certificate covers.

Assume a market-rate PIK coupon and accrue it
